outcome_detail: $1.8 million total settlement — $600,000 to each of the three Jane Doe plaintiffs — reached in September 2022 and finalized by late October 2022.
criminal_detail: No criminal charges were ever filed. Two internal investigations concluded Bailey pressured multiple confidential informants into sexual acts, lied to investigators, and that his actions broke the law, but the statute of limitations on potential misdemeanor charges expired during LMPD's two-year investigation. In February 2023, a Jefferson County grand jury returned a 'no true bill' on sodomy charges presented against Bailey; prosecutors said a Kentucky law in place at the time of the alleged crimes effectively prevented indictment. Bailey resigned from LMPD in 2021.
incident_date_approx: Approximately 2018-2020 (one woman said threats and abuse began with a July 2018 arrest and continued about two years)
description: Three women, proceeding as Jane Does, sued Louisville Metro Government over the conduct of LMPD narcotics detective Brian Bailey — the first filing in October 2020, with a second plaintiff joining in November 2020 and a third in 2021. The suits alleged that Bailey coerced the women into becoming confidential informants and then compelled them to perform sexual acts under threat of criminal prosecution. Internal LMPD investigations concluded that Bailey had pressured multiple informants into sexual acts and lied to investigators. The city settled the claims for $1.8 million in the fall of 2022, split equally among the three women. No criminal charges were filed: limitations periods lapsed during the lengthy investigation, and a grand jury declined in February 2023 to indict Bailey on sodomy charges. Reporting also noted Bailey obtained more residential search warrants than any other LMPD officer between January 2019 and June 2020, nearly all based on informant information.
notes: Filed before 2021 (first complaint October 2020; seed year hint 2021 reflects when the third plaintiff joined); included because resolution occurred in window (settlement 2022).
